transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes (recording appears complete)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Ellen Cho (Redwood SE), Marcus Reyes (CTO, Avalon), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Daniel Ko (SRE), Leanne Ortiz (Product)

Summary:
Quick convergent sync to review this sprint's benchmark delta vs Avalon's incumbent provider. Focus on p95/p99 latency, tail behavior during bursts, throughput under 95th percentile traffic, and one-off tuning (KV caching, batch window). Action items assigned for tracing, a 24-hour dedicated slot, and security follow-up.

Topics covered:
- Latest bench numbers (p95, p99, throughput) vs baseline
- Observed tail spikes and hypothesized causes
- Routing/batching/kv cache tweaks attempted this sprint
- Dedicated slot for 24-hr soak test and access
- Security & compliance questions (data residency, audit logs)

Action items (captured briefly in call): Samir to send spreadsheet; Ellen provision slot; Priya to share real traffic; schedule SOC2 follow-up.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining. we' re on for forty three minutes today. quick check — did the perf team already drop the new numbers in the sheet, Marcus?
[00:18] Marcus: yeah i uploaded an initial dump, it's called "avalon-pilot-july12-latency" — Priya can point you to it. but at a glance we saw readwood... redwood, sorry, redwood's p95 looking much better than incumbent.
[00:30] Priya: yep i shared the link in slack too. there are two sets — steady state and burst. steady state we see median around 55ms for short prompts, p95 about 120ms, p99 around 240ms on Redwood. incumbent is p95 ~220ms, p99 ~410ms.
[00:50] Ellen: okay that's consistent with what we measured in our lab. note though the p99 spikes occur during request coalescence windows when your traffic has microbursts — KV cache cold-starts and slightly suboptimal batching settings show up there.
[01:10] Daniel: i want to call out the tail seems correlated with a few things — large prompt sizes (50-80 tokens), and a pattern of back-to-back inference calls from the same client which inhibits prefix cache hits.
[01:30] Samir: great, can you share an example trace there, Daniel? annotated timestamps? those help us map to the kernel selection and batch cutover.
[01:40] Daniel: yeah i'll export 3 traces from friday's window. they are noisy but i'll annotate.
[01:45] Marcus: remember we also care about sustained throughput — on the incumbent we were seeing 150 rps on the 4xA100 nodes in their setup; Redwood was hitting 180 rps with equivalent slots and slightly lower cost per token.
[02:05] Ellen: we ran a microbenchmark with continuous feeding and saw sustained 185 rps before tail latency degradation. we think increasing the batch window slightly for burst tolerance helped without hurting median latency.
[02:20] Leanne: can you translate that into end-user impact? like chat response feeling laggy? what's acceptable?
[02:28] Marcus: our product target is p95 < 200ms for 95% of chats and p99 < 400ms. so Redwood's numbers look promising but we want to see a 24-hour soak under production-like traffic.
[02:45] Samir: understood. Ellen, can you provision a dedicated slot for a full day test that mirrors Avalon traffic?
[02:53] Ellen: yes, we can. I'll provision a 24-hour dedicated capacity with the same model variant and quant profile we used. I'll share creds and a runbook.
[03:05] Priya: also please make sure the traffic replay keeps the proportion of heavy vs light prompts. otherwise the back-to-back cold prefixes will be underrepresented.
[03:15] Ellen: good call. Priya, can you send the payload histogram and top-10 prompts?
[03:21] Priya: yes i'll upload by end of tomorrow.
[03:25] [crosstalk] Marcus: and include the time-of-day pattern, we see a big surge at 14:00 UTC usually.
[03:33] Samir: noted. on the routing front, one item we pushed this sprint was an adaptive fallback rung — so if batch size hits threshold we shift traffic to a lower-latency variant with slightly higher cost. that reduced tail in lab.
[03:50] Daniel: was that the quantized variant or smaller context window?
[03:55] Ellen: smaller context window first, if latency still degrades we move to a 16-bit quantized variant. the routing policy was conservative.
[04:05] Marcus: any impact on quality when you switch variants? we can't accept hallucination regressions.
[04:12] Ellen: we ran evals against your prompt set — small delta in ROUGE/EM but within your guardrails. we'll attach the eval snapshots. some names were slightly truncated in longer contexts.
[04:28] Leanne: product question: can routing decisions be logged for audit? our compliance folks will want to see when fallback happened.
[04:34] Samir: yes — we record route decisions, model variant changes, and provide trace ids that match the request id. audit logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM.
[04:44] Priya: and KMS? encryption at rest?
[04:47] Samir: yes, keys via customer-managed KMS supported on Private and Dedicated. on Hosted we do envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS for keys.
[04:56] [missed word] Marcus: do you have SOC2 type 2?
[04:59] Samir: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we're happy to share the report under NDA. we'll also do a security deep-dive next week per Leanne's ask.
[05:10] Leanne: yes please, we need an hour with security + privacy.
[05:13] Samir: will schedule.

[05:20] ---- Bench walkthrough (numbers and anomalies) ----
[05:20] Ellen: I'll walk through the sheet: steady-state steady prompts (<= 30 tokens) median 48-60ms, p95 110-130ms. For heavy prompts (50-80 tokens) median 95-130ms, p95 210-260ms. The incumbent had p95 inflated across the board by about +80-100ms. p99s were twice as bad mainly due to cache misses and batch fragmentation.
[06:00] Priya: is that with KV cache warmed?
[06:03] Ellen: steady-state yes, but bursts show cold-start behavior. KV cache is sticky per session, so when clients rotate session ids we lose prefix hits.
[06:15] Daniel: we do rotate session ids for privacy reasons after 6 hours, so we can't rely on indefinite caching.
[06:22] Samir: you can set a session window longer if privacy policies allow. otherwise we can tune prefix weighting and prefetch hot contexts.
[06:30] Marcus: what's the unit-cost delta? we have a hard constraint on cost per 1000 tokens.
[06:36] Ellen: with current batching and quant profile, Redwood estimates unit-cost ~0.85x of incumbent. in many of your scenarios cost is lower because of better batching efficiency.
[06:48] Priya: how reliable is that estimate for spikes?
[06:51] Ellen: spikes drive inefficiency, but our routing fallback was designed to reduce expensive tail mitigation. you'll see a small cost increase during sustained spikes, but net is still lower than incumbent in our sims.

[07:05] ---- Tuning experiments this sprint ----
[07:05] Ellen: we tried three knobs: batch window +10ms, early-cutoff for oversized prompts, and a more aggressive KV prefetch on warm contexts. Batch window change reduced tail lat by ~12% in microbench. Prefetch reduced some cold misses but increased memory footprint.
[07:30] Daniel: memory footprint concern — do you have caps per slot? we want predictable OOM behavior.
[07:36] Samir: yes, we cap and provide metrics; if memory crosses threshold the runtime rejects new large batches to preserve stability. we'll show these metrics in the console.

[07:50] Priya: curious about quantization — we saw artifacts on a couple hallucination tests in your early quant runs last month. are those resolved?
[07:58] Ellen: we moved to a hybrid quant approach for those model families; quality delta is negligible for your prompts. we'll include eval diffs and the exact quant profile.

[08:20] ---- Soak test plan ----
[08:20] Samir: plan: 24-hour dedicated slot, replay production-like traffic including time-of-day spikes and heavy prompts. Need top-10 prompts and histogram from Priya. Ellen provisions slot and we'll run overnight. We will run two variants: 1) baseline config used this week, 2) routing-enabled config with fallback. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, OOMs, dropped requests, and unit-cost.
[08:50] Marcus: and application-level metrics — think time-to-first-token as well.
[08:55] Samir: yes we'll include TTF token and end-to-end from client to response.

[09:05] ---- Observability and traces ----n[09:05] Daniel: make sure span ids match — we use jaeger internally. can you push traces to our collector?
[09:12] Ellen: we can export traces in OTLP and link trace ids to Redwood request ids. will need your collector endpoint and creds.
[09:20] Daniel: i'll send the endpoint.

[09:25] ---- Questions from Avalon ----
[09:25] Leanne: what's the rollback plan if we see quality regressions in the soak?
[09:30] Samir: we keep the incumbent route as a warm fallback; during the soak if quality dips we'll automatically fallback per policy and open a ticket. We'll also snapshot model versions and you can pin to previous variant.
[09:42] Marcus: curious about multi-region routing — can we place inference closer to EU users?
[09:48] Ellen: yes, region routing supported. For the pilot we used us-west but we can spin up eu-west nodes for a segmented test.
[09:55] Priya: any changes required on our side for VPC peering later?
[09:58] Samir: for private deployment yes you'll need VPC peering and routes; for Dedicated we handle secure tunnels. We'll send a checklist.

[10:08] ---- Minor transcript noise: speaker label glitch for a minute ----
[10:08] Speaker 1: [unintelligible]
[10:12] Samir: i think that was a quick drop, ignore.

[10:20] Ellen: last engineering note — in our next run we'll instrument per-token latency breakdown so you can see transformer layers that spike. that helped another customer identify an attention kernel mismatch on older GPU drivers.
[10:40] Daniel: good. please include driver versions in the runbook. we had a mismatch before which explained +30ms in p95.

[10:55] ---- Recap and next steps ----
[10:55] Samir: recap — Ellen provisions 24-hour dedicated slot, Priya shares traffic/profile and top prompts, Daniel shares tracer endpoint and 3 annotated traces, I'll send the latency vs baseline spreadsheet and SOC2 NDA link. Security deep-dive scheduled next week. Any other items?
[11:20] Leanne: please also include a short note on fallback logging export format so our auditors can consume it.
[11:27] Samir: will include.
[11:30] Marcus: thanks all, excited to run the soak.
[11:35] Samir: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar holds and the artifacts.
[11:40] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-recognition of Redwood product names ("readwood"), some timestamps fuzzy where network jitter caused slight gaps. Cued files: sheet link (avalon-pilot-july12-latency), eval snapshots, annotated traces to be uploaded by Avalon.
